newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil to cut 3.1 bln reais from 1997 budget.
newsitem.headline: Brazil to cut 3.1 bln reais from 1997 budget.

text.p: Brazil will cut 3.1 billion reais in spending from its 1997 budget in order to ensure a federal government's primary surplus this year of 0.8 percent of gross domestic product, said Planning Minister Antonio Kandir.

Kandir told reporters that 1.6 billion reais of the cuts was basically due to the lower inflation forecast for the year, which had originally been put at 10.6 percent and is now expected at 6.3 percent.
He said another 1.0 billion reais will be physical cuts in planned maintenance costs and another 500 million in budgeted investments.
Kandir said the government was serious about its objective of 0.8 percent primary surplus of the GDP for the central government and the Central Bank.
"I would like to make it clear that we will strive for this commitment no matter the circumstances," Kandir said.

Kandir and Finance Minister Pedro Malan were sending a decree outlining the 1997 budget spending plan, including amended expenditure and revenue targets, to President Fernando Henrique Cardoso later Friday.
